My first project involved setting up a new application in a new system, and I needed to work with a new tool that was unfamiliar to me. Birger Møller-Jensen: A Story of a Family first appeared in a British newspaper in 2017, and I realized that the way I approach a job is shaped by the way I interact with people. That interest has stayed with me, and I have been drawn to the way conversations turn into practical decisions. I began my Bachelor’s degree at a university not listed in the major cities, and I completed 4 projects with tangible outcomes. The first one was a family-focused project that helped me understand how to use my own experiences to build a better service. The second was a practical workshop that helped me understand how to close a gap in a market, and the last one was a tenant-focused project that helped me think through how to build a service that works for both customers and partners.

My interest in sales has deepened through observation and reflection. For example, when I started work in a new area, I started using a new tool and fell in love with it. In one day, I was working on a topic that was not on my radar, and I quickly learned how to use it effectively. Few additions can match the power of a good order, the satisfaction of seeing a group of people working together, or the satisfaction of seeing a website, a delivery, or a shipment moving. Originally from Kenya, I hold a Bachelor’s degree from a university not listed in the major global rankings, and I have completed 2 projects with tangible outcomes. In one of those projects, I worked on a logistics coordination process that was slow, error-prone, and took more than a year to get to the next stage. In another, I was hand-on in day-to-day operations, so when a team of users, suppliers, and carriers needed a shared view of a shipment, I helped ensure everyone was tracking the right way.

What matters most to me is how it connects with my professional development. Coordinating the flow of shipments, orders, and deliveries is a constant challenge, but I value the way it builds trust and builds my ability to work with a team. In one setting, a trusted team member would not be able to follow a shared tracking process when a team of users, carriers, and suppliers were working at the same time. I have also been known to work through repetitive tracking issues, such as when a team of carriers had to wait for a shipment to arrive, and I helped ensure the team was on the same page. I am also interested in becoming a Logistics Coordinator, someone who can bring a clear understanding of logistics coordination to a busy area and work with a few trusted partners to ensure the flow of shipments, orders, and deliveries is kept to a manageable pace.

What first held my attention about web development was the way a simple idea could become something useful, interactive, and accessible on a screen. That blend of creativity and logic is still what drives me: I enjoy turning complex user needs into smooth digital experiences that make everyday tasks easier. Over time, this interest grew into a wider fascination with how websites and applications are structured, improved, and used in real life. I am now seeking to build my career as a Web Developer because it brings together my interest in building practical digital products with my focus on clean, user-friendly solutions, strong front-end development, performance, and usability. Currently, I hold a Bachelor’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 500, and across my work and study I have completed 5 projects with tangible outcomes, each reinforcing my commitment to creating web experiences that are functional, scalable, and intuitive.

My approach to work has been shaped by practical experience. In one role, I needed to use a new tool that was central to the team’s workflow, and after a few months of focused effort I was contributing independently to day-to-day tasks with it. On another project, a recurring issue was slowing the team down, so I put together a workable alternative process that reduced the disruption and helped us keep delivery moving. Colleagues have also sometimes come to me with questions in my own area, including asking me to look over front-end implementation choices or help untangle smaller technical issues during active work. I am originally from Ethiopia, and alongside my professional goals I value the personal side of building technology. One of my favourite memories is showing my family a website I had built for a local business and watching them excitedly place a test order just to see it work in real time. That moment stayed with me because it captured exactly why I want to keep building for the web: every line of code should lead to a clear, useful experience for real people.

Nothing is more satisfying to me than restoring something essential and seeing the result immediately, especially when that result is safe, reliable power for the people who depend on it. That is what drew me to becoming an electrician: the practical challenge of finding faults, putting them right, and knowing that reliable power improves everyday life in direct, meaningful ways. What began as a fascination with how things work has grown into a career focused on keeping homes, businesses, and people connected. I am originally from the Netherlands, and I bring to my work the same commitment to steady progress that supported me through a Doctorate at a university ranked in the global top 100. Across my career, I have completed 5 projects with tangible outcomes, each reinforcing how much I value work that can be seen, tested, and relied upon. One of my favourite family memories is showing a relative a building I had helped wire, only for the lights to come on just as I explained my role; it turned an ordinary moment into a lasting reminder that this job creates something real.

My professional foundation has been built through practical electrical work and continued learning. When I needed to use a new diagnostic tool and become familiar with a related technical area, I did not master it overnight; instead, I built confidence over more than a year of regular use on routine jobs until it became part of my normal working practice. In day-to-day fault-finding, I work carefully through established procedures to identify and resolve issues safely and efficiently, and when an unusual case falls outside the normal pattern, I make a point of seeking guidance before proceeding. That approach has helped me diagnose faults quickly and accurately while keeping downtime to a minimum. At the same time, colleagues have occasionally come to me with questions in my own area, such as checking a testing sequence or confirming the likely cause of a recurring fault, and I have been glad to talk it through with them. I am now eager to bring this practical mindset, grounded training, and genuine enthusiasm for electrical work to my next role as an electrician.

A strong visual identity can change the way people feel, understand, and connect long before a single word is read. It is this belief that drew me to graphic design and continues to shape the way I approach creative work: I want to produce visuals that are not only striking, but purposeful and memorable. Originally from Peru, I built my academic foundation through a Doctorate at a university ranked in the global top 100, an experience that strengthened the research, structure, and disciplined thinking I bring to creative projects. Across my work, I have completed 8 projects with tangible outcomes, each requiring me to turn broad concepts into clear visual systems that could work consistently across print, digital, and brand touchpoints. In particular, I became increasingly interested in how abstract ideas can be distilled into cohesive identities that people immediately recognise and respond to, which confirmed for me that graphic design was the right professional path.

Alongside this, I have learned to adapt quickly in practical settings. On one project, I needed to use a new design tool that the team had recently adopted; within a few weeks I was using it confidently in live work, and soon after that I was helping colleagues get started when they asked how to handle layouts and shared assets. In another role, repeated delays were being caused by a file-handoff issue between design and production, so I set up a simpler naming and export process that reduced confusion and helped the team move work forward more smoothly. I also value working closely with others and sharing knowledge in a straightforward way when it is useful.

Beyond my academic and professional development, one of my favourite memories came during a family visit to a local café where I had recently redesigned the branding. My family immediately pointed out the menu, signage, and packaging before I said anything, and seeing them interact so naturally with something I had created reminded me that good design becomes part of everyday life. Altogether, these experiences have prepared me to contribute thoughtfully as a Graphic Designer while continuing to grow through purposeful, engaging visual communication.

Reliable results often depend on work that happens quietly, carefully, and with full respect for process, and that is exactly what draws me to laboratory work. My natural curiosity about how things work, combined with a desire to contribute to accurate, meaningful results, has led me toward a career as a Laboratory Technician, where careful testing supports wider scientific and healthcare goals. I am especially motivated by the idea that precision behind the scenes can make a real difference in research, quality, and patient outcomes. This aligns closely with the way I like to work: maintaining accuracy under pressure, whether preparing samples or documenting results with consistency and care so that the wider team can rely on each stage of testing. Therefore, I seek to build on my foundation through practical laboratory work informed by my Master’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 500, with the long-term goal of contributing to dependable testing and high-quality scientific outcomes. Originally from Ethiopia, I bring that background as part of my personal journey while grounding my professional focus firmly in the laboratory environment.

I have been fortunate to grow in an environment where careful work and genuine enthusiasm could be shared at home as well as at work. One of my favourite family memories is coming home after a busy week in the lab and discovering that my younger sibling had turned our kitchen into a “mini lab,” carefully labelling cups of juice like test samples; it was a funny but proud reminder that my connection to methodical work and discovery was visible to my family too. In my professional experience, I completed 3 projects with tangible outcomes, each reinforcing the importance of dependable processes and clear results. In one role, I needed to use a new laboratory tool and related subject area, and after a few months of focused effort I was able to use it productively in routine work. When a recurring issue was slowing the team down, I helped put in place a practical workaround that reduced delays and kept testing moving. Colleagues also sometimes came to me with questions in my own area, and I valued being able to talk through procedures and help them move forward. It is with this experience that I am ready to contribute careful, consistent, and meaningful support as a Laboratory Technician.

What continues to draw me to hotel management is the way thoughtful service can shape how people remember a journey long after they have checked out. A well-run hotel does more than provide a room; it creates ease, comfort, and confidence for guests while giving staff a clear, supportive environment in which to do their best work. That is why I have chosen to build my career in hospitality, with a focus on creating welcoming, seamless guest experiences and maintaining the calm, polished standards that encourage guests to return. I am originally from Ethiopia, and I hold a Bachelor’s degree from a university not listed in the major global rankings. During my studies, I completed 2 projects with tangible outcomes, which strengthened my interest in practical, results-focused work and confirmed that I wanted a career where attention to detail and coordination matter every day.

Over time, I have built my approach to hotel operations through steady learning and hands-on experience. When I first needed to use a new hotel management tool, I did not master it immediately; instead, I spent more than a year using it regularly for bookings, reporting, and service follow-up until it became a comfortable part of my daily routine. In day-to-day operations, I work through issues by following established procedures carefully, whether resolving scheduling gaps or handling routine guest concerns, and when an unusual case falls outside normal practice, I make sure to seek guidance so it is handled properly. Colleagues have at times come to me with questions in my own area, such as room coordination or service processes, and I have been glad to talk through the steps with them. My connection to hospitality is also personal: during a family stay at a sister property, my relatives began pointing out small service touches they recognised from stories I had shared, turning the visit into a light-hearted “hotel manager’s eye” challenge. That moment reinforced for me how meaningful careful hospitality can be, and I am eager to bring that same commitment, consistency, and guest focus to a Hotel Manager role.

Every strong business relationship begins with a conversation that makes someone feel understood. That is what drew me to a career as a Sales Representative: I genuinely enjoy connecting with people, understanding what they need, and helping them find solutions that make their work or daily life easier. The combination of relationship-building and measurable impact is what makes sales both personally rewarding and professionally motivating for me. One of my favourite memories was bringing my family to a company open house, where my younger sibling listened to me chat with customers and later joked that I could “make friends with anyone in five minutes.” It became a running family story, and it captured why this profession feels like such a natural fit. Originally from the Netherlands, I bring that same people-focused approach to every professional interaction, aiming to build trust quickly by listening carefully, asking the right questions, and shaping each conversation around the customer’s priorities.

My academic background includes a Doctorate completed at a university ranked in the global top 100, where I worked on 3 completed projects with tangible outcomes. That experience taught me how to move ideas into results and communicate clearly with different audiences. During one period of focused work, I needed to use a new tool outside my usual experience, and within a few months I was using it productively in day-to-day project delivery. In another role, my team kept losing time to a recurring process issue, so I put together a practical workaround that reduced delays and gave us a more reliable way to keep work moving.
